# Media processing security

## Upgrade instructions

Upgrade both the PHP and cron images:

```sh
kvsctl check
kvsctl upgrade
```

This release needs no `kvsctl` newer than 26.10.4 and introduces no database
migration. Wait for active conversions to finish before recreating the
containers. Updating the CLI alone does not install these protections.

From the installation's Compose directory, check the installed images:

```sh
docker compose exec -T -u www-data php-fpm kvs-media-security-check
docker compose exec -T -u www-data cron kvs-media-security-check
```

Apply the [official KVS media security patch](https://kernel-scripts.com/updates/media-security-6.3.0-7.0.3_patch.zip)
to the CMS separately, following the vendor's instructions. This stack
release does not replace or overwrite the site's PHP source files. Remote
conversion servers and standalone installations need their own updates or
mitigations; upgrading this Docker stack does not change those servers.

## FFmpeg

Both images rebuild Debian's FFmpeg packages with the MagicYUV and TDSC
decoders disabled. The restriction is compiled into `libavcodec`, so it
also applies to `ffprobe`, absolute binary paths and callers of the shared
library. It cannot be undone by changing an FFmpeg command-line option.
The locally rebuilt packages carry a `+kvs1` version suffix and preserve
Debian's other codec features and library ABI.
The complete modified source and rebuild instructions ship with each image
under `/usr/local/share/kvs-ffmpeg-source/`.

Debian 13 fixes [CVE-2026-8461](https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-8461)
in FFmpeg 7.1.5, but still tracks
[CVE-2026-65703](https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-65703)
as vulnerable in that version. Merely rebuilding an image with the current
distribution packages would therefore leave TDSC decoding exposed.

MagicYUV and TDSC input videos are deliberately unsupported in this release.
The ordinary H.264, HEVC and AV1 conversion paths remain available.

## ImageMagick

The distribution's resource limits remain in place. Additional coder,
module and delegate restrictions block PostScript, EPS, PDF and XPS
processing, including a PostScript document renamed with a `.jpg`
extension. This prevents the affected document readers from reaching
Ghostscript, the component affected by
[CVE-2026-101258](https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-101258).

JPEG, PNG, WebP and AVIF processing remain available. Applications relying
on document-to-image conversion must use a separately maintained service
instead of these KVS media containers.

## Verification

Every PHP and cron image build runs `kvs-media-security-check` as the site's
unprivileged user. It checks that both decoders are absent, that a harmless
MagicYUV AVI cannot be decoded, and that a PostScript document disguised as
JPEG is rejected specifically by the security policy. It also encodes and
decodes H.264, HEVC and AV1 with AAC, extracts a screenshot, and creates and
resizes JPEG, PNG, WebP and AVIF images.

These checks validate the restrictions and ordinary media processing. They
do not execute a remote-code-execution payload or audit a site for previous
compromise. Rolling back to an older stack image removes these protections.

The image restrictions, build checks and refreshed base image digests are
implemented in [ed16872](https://github.com/MaximeMichaud/KVS-install/commit/ed168721aa98fdde45894cd8c04217215f4c64f9).

[Full comparison with 26.10.5](https://github.com/MaximeMichaud/KVS-install/compare/26.10.5...26.11.0)
